title: Parallel circuits
target: Relate branch currents to a shared potential difference.
criteria: Identify branches connected across the same two nodes.
Use equal voltage across parallel branches.
Add branch currents to find supply current.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A 4 Ω resistor and an 8 Ω resistor each connect directly between the same two nodes. What arrangement is this?
cpa.guide: Parallel elements share both endpoint nodes.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: One branch of an ideal parallel circuit opens. Other branches remain connected across an ideal constant-voltage supply. What can happen?
options: The other branches continue carrying their previous currents.
The voltage of every other branch must double.
Current must cross the open branch.
cpa.guide: The other complete paths remain across the same ideal supply voltage.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Resistors of 5 Ω and 10 Ω connect in parallel across 15 V. What voltage is across each?
options: 5 V across one and 10 V across the other.
cpa.guide: Both connect to the same two supply nodes.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 16 Ω branch is connected across an 8 V ideal supply. What is branch current?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Three outgoing parallel branch currents are 0.40 A, 0.25 A, and 0.15 A. What is supply current?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 12 V ideal supply feeds 4 Ω and 12 Ω parallel resistors. Which total-current calculation is correct?
options: Both branches carry 3 A, so total is 6 A.
cpa.guide: Branch currents are 3 and 1 A. Add currents; do not add parallel resistances directly.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
